summary: This Dockerfile creates an Ubuntu container with Zsh shell, Git, and curl installed. It then sets up Oh-My-Zsh with the autosuggestions plugin, pre-populates some shell history for convenience, customizes the prompt to show a whale emoji indicating we're in a container, and starts an interactive login shell by default.

explanations.3: This prevents Docker from prompting for user input during package installation, which would hang the build since there's no interactive terminal.
explanations.6: The --no-install-recommends flag installs only the essential packages we requested, not optional dependencies, which keeps the image smaller.
explanations.11: After installing packages, we delete the apt cache files to reduce the final image size, since they're only needed during installation.
explanations.14: This downloads and runs the Oh-My-Zsh installer script directly from GitHub; the curl flags make it fail on errors and run silently.
explanations.15: The --unattended flag runs the installer without prompting, and --keep-zshrc preserves any existing configuration file.
explanations.18: The --depth=1 flag does a shallow clone, downloading only the latest commit instead of the entire history, which is faster and smaller.
explanations.20: This uses sed to find the line starting with 'plugins=(git)' and adds 'zsh-autosuggestions' to that list so the plugin is actually enabled.
explanations.24: The printf command writes multiple lines to the history file; each line follows Zsh's history format with a fake timestamp and command.
explanations.31: This appends a custom prompt to the Zshrc file; %B makes it bold, %F{color} sets the foreground color, and %n and %~ are placeholders for username and current directory.
explanations.33: The -i flag starts an interactive shell, -l makes it a login shell (which reads startup files), and this becomes the default command when the container starts.
